review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally encode the remaining row indices for one elimination column as a finite search domain. Construct a reversible predicate marking only the index that Python's max operation on abs(rows[i][col]) would select, including its first-index tie behavior and any relevant binary64 comparison behavior. Run the search once per column, decode and classically verify the index, then retain the classical zero-pivot check, row swap, elimination, and back substitution.

Encode indices col through n-1 in a basis-state register, with invalid encodings unmarked. Supply coherent access to the active column of the current mutable augmented rows and exact representations of its binary64 values. The oracle must reversibly reproduce absolute-value comparisons, selection ordering, first-index ties, and applicable exceptional floating-point states. Data loading, synchronization after each elimination update, arithmetic workspace, and uncomputation remain unresolved.

The predicate can mark exactly one selected index for each nonempty remaining range; in an all-zero column it must select the first remaining row so the existing classical zero-pivot check raises ValueError.
Overflow, infinities, or NaNs arising during elimination complicate faithful reproduction of Python's comparison and eventual exception behavior.
This plan records only a conditional structural formulation. It does not establish semantic equivalence, practical suitability, benchmark support, or quantum advantage.

binding.rationale: The revision narrows the candidate to line13 and requires reproducing Python max, but supplies no actual comparator formula or ordered update recurrence. Unique marking is still an assumed obligation and exceptional-state handling unresolved. Do not invent a selector by expanding the target operation or add a finite-only guard; retain insufficient evidence for this replacement relation. Scope, implementation, fallback and whole-task claims remain separate.
